body:
Hi @lukasavic,

Which version of react-instantsearch are you currently using?

On the last version, the URL Syncing has to be implemented by the user typically to allow more advance use cases like yours. To synchronize an `InstantSearch` with an URL you need to handle the `InstantSearch` state externally like described here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/v2/docgen/src/guide/Routing.md.
You can also find the guide about multiple indices here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/v2/docgen/src/guide/Multi%20index.md

Be careful, the API described in those guides has not been entirely released yet so I suggest you wait for a couple of days before trying it. Those guides will also be available [on our documentation website](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/react/).

Basically the idea is to listen to every state changes for both indices and create your URL accordingly. Then, when you'll need to update the `InstantSearch` state, you will take your url and  reconstruct the state based on your previous conventions.
